subject: Renewal + capacity uplift: 12mo commit, quantization pilot & latency benchmarks
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@novusai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Q1 renewal — usage review & capacity ask

Hi Marissa,

We’re starting renewal planning for our Jan–Dec usage and wanted to get a quick health check from you. Headline items:

- Q4 token spend was ~18% above forecast (see attached export).
- Latency for our high-concurrency endpoints drifted by ~40–60ms during peak windows on Dec 15–22.
- We’re evaluating whether to move to a 12mo committed contract with a 20% higher baseline and a short quantization pilot to reduce unit cost.

Can we schedule a 30–45 min review this week? Prefer Tue or Wed morning PT. Also attaching our usage CSV and the latency screenshot from Datadog.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of ML Ops, NovusAI
elena@novusai.com
attachments: redwood_usage_q4_2027.csv (csv), latency_screenshots_dec2027.png (image)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 renewal — usage review & capacity ask

Elena — thanks for the data, and for the heads-up. Confirmed that I pulled the downstream usage files; initial read below and I’ve attached a short latency audit (pdf) and a proposed addendum for the 12mo commit so we have a working doc to iterate on.

Quick initial assessment (Q4 2027):
- Net tokens: 1.9B tokens total; 18% above your projection driven by two bursts tied to A/B experiment traffic on Dec 16–18.
- Model mix: 62% gen-text at longer contexts (avg seq len +15%), explains higher token consumption.
- Latency: production p95 moved from ~220ms -> ~270–285ms during peak; root cause looks like concurrent KV cache misses during model warmups.

Proposed next steps before the call:
1) Run a 4-week quantization pilot on a subset of endpoints (we estimate ~18–24% cost reduction with negligible quality loss on your evaluation set).
2) Add a 12mo baseline commit (20% uplift) + a 3-month burst credit pool to cover experiments.
3) Schedule a 45-min walkthrough where we:
   - walk through the latency audit,
   - align on the pilot scope and success metrics (token savings, latency delta, quality thresholds),
   - agree on commercial terms for the addendum.

Can you confirm availability Wed 22 Feb 09:30–10:15 PT or Thu 23 Feb 08:00–08:45 PT?

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben/ Karthik on pricing and legal redline considerations.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
attachments: latency_report_q4_2027.pdf (pdf), proposed_commit_addendum_v2.docx (docx)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 renewal — pricing options + credits

Marissa / Karthik — quick price note:

- Baseline: If they commit to +20% baseline for 12mo we can offer a blended rate at 8.5 ¢/k token (vs current 10.2 ¢).
- Pilot: Quantization pilot we can offer at no incremental infra charge (tech support included) if they accept a short reporting cadence (weekly short evals).
- Burst credits: recommend 50k credits to start (covers ~2 weeks of experiment surges), refundable as usage credits if committed volume is met.

Would like to keep the addendum simple: 12mo term, baseline tokens, burst credits, pilot appendix, and an SLA clause that maps to latency rollback triggers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 renewal — allocation math

Agree with Ben. A few notes on economics and ops:
- If quantization reduces model size / memory pressure we should see p95 latency improvements of ~10–20ms during sustained load; KV-cache warmups still need a separate mitigation (we can propose a tiny prewarm TTL for critical endpoints).
- Financial: the blended rate + burst credits keeps ARR predictable while protecting them from immediate overage shock.
- Legal: add a 30-day rollback window in the SLA appendix for sustained latency regressions.

I’ll prepare a short one-pager to include in the addendum that spells out pilot success criteria and rollback triggers.

Karthik
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Mar 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal & next steps — NovusAI (NVX-2028-1379)

Elena — thanks for the call last week. Per our discussion, here is a concise recap and the proposed path forward:

Key takeaways
- Q4 overage driver: A/B experiments increased gen-text tokens and sequence lengths resulting in +18% token spend.
- Latency root cause: KV cache misses during model warmups; expected mitigation via a small prewarm TTL + targeted quantization pilot.

Commercial proposal
- 12-month term starting Apr 1, 2028. Baseline commit = current monthly average * 1.20.
- Blended unit rate: 8.5 ¢/k token.
- Burst credit pool: 50k credits available for the first 90 days for experiments (convertible to usage credits if committed volume is achieved).
- Quantization pilot: 4-week technical pilot on staging -> canary -> prod path. Weekly checkpoints and a small quality eval suite (we will provide).
- SLA appendix: 30-day rollback clause if p95 latency regresses >50ms post-change (excludes external infra incidents).

Attachments & links
- latency_report_q4_2027.pdf — detailed timing windows and callouts
- redwood_usage_q4_2027.csv — your raw export (we annotated key bursts)
- proposed_commit_addendum_v2.docx — commercial/legal draft
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/1379

Requested next steps
1) Please confirm internal approval path and any procurement timelines.
2) If acceptable, mark the addendum as "Draft OK" and I’ll route to legal for a tracked redline.
3) We’ll kick the quantization pilot the week after signatures and share a short onboarding checklist.

If you want, I can hop on a 20-min call with Procurement and your ML Ops engineering lead to walk the pilot acceptance criteria.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Office: +1 415-555-0123
